findings.source_quote: εἱστήκεισαν δὲ εἰς τὰ τέσσαρα μέρη τῆς πύλης, ἀνὰ μέσον αὐτῶν ἀνὰ δύο παρθένοι.
findings.english_quote: They stood on the gate’s four sides, with two virgins between each pair of them.
findings.issue: The translation follows the selected αὐτῶν, but the notes do not disclose the supplied apparatus report that A reads αὐτῆς instead. This is a consequential pronoun alternative in the description of the virgins’ arrangement, not merely a spelling difference. The apparatus attributes support for the working reading to versions; the English documentation leaves that source choice unexplained.
findings.suggested_revision: Retain the working translation and add a bounded textual note, for example: “The selected printed Greek reads ‘between them’ (αὐτῶν), which the supplied apparatus reports as supported by versions. A is reported to read αὐτῆς, ‘of/between it,’ changing the pronoun’s reference.” Do not present the reported reading as freshly verified manuscript evidence. Review the proposed note before adoption.

findings.source_quote: ὅσα γὰρ οὐ δύνασαι νοῆσαι, μὴ ἐπιχείρει, συνετὸς ὤν
findings.english_quote: Do not attempt what you cannot understand as though you were wise.
findings.issue: The English accurately preserves the working text’s inability and prohibition, but its documentation omits the supplied apparatus distinction between printed οὐ δύνασαι and A’s reported οὐδὲ. Footnote c discusses only συνετὸς ὤν, leaving undisclosed the version-supported working wording underlying “cannot understand.”
findings.suggested_revision: Keep the selected working reading and add a textual note identifying οὐ δύνασαι (‘you cannot’) as the printed reading supported by the versions listed in the supplied apparatus, while A is reported to have οὐδὲ (‘nor/not even’) instead. Explain that this report alone does not establish a complete alternative English sentence; do not silently reconstruct or replace the working text. Review the new note separately.

findings.source_quote: εἱστήκεισαν δὲ εἰς τὰ τέσσαρα μέρη τῆς πύλης, ἀνὰ μέσον αὐτῶν ἀνὰ δύο παρθένοι.
findings.english_quote: Two virgins stood between each pair of the four, along the gate’s four sides.
findings.issue: Independently checked against the selected Greek, this arrangement is compatible with αὐτῶν. However, the simplified edition’s notes omit the supplied apparatus alternative αὐτῆς reported for A and do not disclose that the working pronoun is supported by versions. The alternative affects reference within the arrangement description.
findings.suggested_revision: Retain the working translation and add an accessible textual note distinguishing selected αὐτῶν (‘between them’) from A’s reported αὐτῆς (‘of/between it’). Attribute the information to the supplied printed-apparatus transcription rather than claiming direct manuscript verification. Review the proposed note before adoption.

findings.source_quote: ὅσα γὰρ οὐ δύνασαι νοῆσαι, μὴ ἐπιχείρει, συνετὸς ὤν
findings.english_quote: Do not try to understand what you cannot grasp as though you were wise.
findings.issue: The simplified wording preserves the selected prohibition and inability, but the accompanying notes do not disclose that the supplied apparatus reports οὐδὲ for A where the working printed text has οὐ δύνασαι. The existing lexical note addresses the wisdom expression, not this consequential source distinction.
findings.suggested_revision: Retain “cannot grasp” and add a bounded note explaining that the selected printed Greek has ‘you cannot,’ supported by the versions listed in the supplied apparatus, whereas A is reported to have ‘nor/not even.’ Avoid inventing a complete reconstructed alternative sentence from that isolated report. Review the proposed note separately.

summary: Both editions cover the selected passage and preserve its visionary assertions, negations, speaker distinctions, and instruction to ask the Lord. Revision is needed to disclose two consequential working-reading alternatives explicitly supplied in the apparatus evidence. The existing Amherst notes appropriately distinguish partial preservation from supplied letters and avoid claiming complete witness support. This review evaluates the supplied Greek and attributed reports, not unseen manuscript images or exhaustive collation; it does not require replacing the disclosed working text.
